rounds.text: Coforge Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental momentum, evidenced by a compound sales growth of 29% and a compound profit growth of 29% over the last five years [E15, E19]. This top- and bottom-line expansion accelerates further in the trailing twelve months, where sales surged by 42% and profit leaped by 92% [E17, E21]. Operational quality underpins these gains, highlighted by a robust Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 23.5% and a Return on Equity (ROE) of 21.4% [E12, E13], alongside a healthy cash conversion of 1.03x that ensures reported profits are fully backed by operating cash flows of Rs 1,792 Cr [E34, E35]. Market strength confirms this operational outperformance, as the stock commands a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and earns a high-confidence BUY score of 90 out of 100 on the rules-based screen [E49, E50, E64]. Conceded: the company trades at an elevated P/E of 41.8x, sits 95% of the way up its 52-week range, and carries a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to a negative margin of safety [E1, E44, E47].

Coforge Ltd trades at an elevated valuation that lacks support from its discounted cash flow model, which places intrinsic value at Rs 1,931 per share against a higher market price of Rs 2,047, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -6.0% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the current market price implies an aggressive earnings growth expectation of 18.8%, which outpaces the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E46]. Financial risk has escalated noticeably as borrowings surged dramatically to Rs 6,026 Cr in September 2026, up sharply from just Rs 728 Cr a year earlier [E39]. This heavy debt accumulation coincides with concerning quality flags in the filed statements, specifically noting that the tax rate seems low and that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E62, E63]. Institutional backing has also eroded over the longer term, with foreign institutional holdings dropping from 34.04% in December 2023 to 24.75% in September 2026, and domestic institutional holdings falling from 55.02% to 43.79% over the same period [E41, E42]. Conceded: [E14], [E18], [E21], [E35], [E36].

Conceded: [E44], [E45], [E46]. While the DCF and reverse DCF models display tight margins, they ignore stellar fundamental momentum where compounded profit growth reached 92% over the trailing twelve months and sales grew 42% [E17, E21]. The surge in borrowings to Rs 6,026 Cr [E39] must be contextualized against robust operating cash flow of Rs 1,792 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1,197 Cr in March 2026, with cash conversion fully backing profits at 1.03x [E34, E35, E36]. Regarding institutional erosion over the longer horizon [E41, E42], recent institutional money flow reads as POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with a holding increase of 1.61 percentage points [E43]. Conceded: [E62], [E63]. The company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 36.0% and rules-based screens score the equity at 90 out of 100 with high confidence [E60, E64].

Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E60]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 1,792 Cr and cash conversion is 1.03x, borrowings surged nearly eightfold from Rs 728 Cr to Rs 6,026 Cr in Sep 2026, introducing significant financial leverage that cannot be dismissed by cash flows alone [E39]. Conceded: [E43]. Despite recent positive institutional money flow, long-term institutional backing has experienced severe erosion, with foreign holdings dropping from 34.04% in Dec 2023 to 24.75% and domestic holdings falling from 55.02% to 43.79% [E41, E42]. The bull’s reliance on TTM sales and profit growth of 42% and 92% ignores rules-based warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E17, E21, E69]. Furthermore, the company's low tax rate and potential capitalization of interest costs flag clear accounting quality risks [E62, E63]. Finally, even if rules-based screens score the equity high, quantitative screen reasons explicitly flag decelerating earnings alongside a negative -6.0% margin of safety from discounted cash flow models [E45, E64, E69].

Conceded: [E39]. While borrowings surged to Rs 6,026 Cr in Sep 2026, the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.27x and generated robust operating cash flow of Rs 1,792 Cr with full cash conversion at 1.03x [E34, E35, E37]. Conceded: [E41, E42]. Although long-term institutional ownership has shifted, recent institutional money flow reads positive with a holding increase of 1.61 percentage points [E43]. The bear's worry about decelerating earnings ignores extraordinary trailing growth of 42% in sales and 92% in profit, alongside a high-confidence rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 that firmly designates the company a buy [E17, E21, E64, E69]. Furthermore, fundamental outperformance invalidates valuation cautions, as 5-year profit growth of 29% heavily outpaces 5-year price growth of 14% [E55].

Conceded: [E34, E35, E37]. Despite robust cash flow generation and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.27x, borrowings still escalated dramatically to Rs 6,026 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 728 Cr a year prior, accompanied by flags for potential interest capitalization and low tax rates [E39, E62, E63]. While the bull points to recent institutional inflows, long-term institutional confidence has undeniably eroded with foreign holdings dropping from 34.04% to 24.75% and domestic holdings falling from 55.02% to 43.79% [E41, E42, E43]. Furthermore, the appeal to trailing growth metrics masks the explicit screen warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E17, E21, E69]. Finally, dismissing valuation cautions is untenable when a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1,931 against a market price of Rs 2,047, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -6.0% while sitting at 95% of its 52-week range [E44, E45, E47].
